sentences.text: The Committal Court i.e. the Court of learned SDJM, Darrang he should process against the present petitioners and apprehending their arrest, the present petitioners approached the Court learned Additional Sessions Judge (FTC) Darrang praying of grant of anticipatory bail.

Thereafter, on 06.06.2023, the petitioners, Habej Ali filed an application bearing No. 3659/2023,
showing his cause of absence before the learned Committal Court, however, the said application was rejected and learned Committal Court issued warrant of arrest against the petitioners as well as other absentee co-accused including the first petitioner, namely Sahid Ali therefore, apprehending the arrest the present petitioners have approached this Court seeking an order under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that merely filing of charge-sheet is in itself is not a bar in exercising power of this Court under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and even after charge- sheet is filed, this Court may issue order under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, if it finds that the petitioners are apprehending their arrest and in support of the said contention learned counsel has relied of the ruling of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India "Bharat Choudhury and Another VBs. State of Bihar and Another" reported in 2003 8 SSC 78.
Page No.# 1/5 vs The State Of Assam on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170565915/
2 Page No.# 4/5 Learned counsel for the petitioner has also relied on the ruling of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Mahdoom Bava Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation (Order dated 20.03.2023 passed in SLP Crl. No. 376/2023) wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India observed that in some part of the country there seems to be a practice followed in courts to remand the accused to custody the moment, they appear in response to summons.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that in the instant case, the charge-sheet has been laid,
inter-alia, under Section 307 of the Indian Penal Code, also where the maximum punishment is imprisonment for life for which normally the Committal Court due to embargo of Section 437 clause 1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, read with Section 209 (a) & (b) of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 remands the accused custody if they are not on bail even if they appear before the trial Court in response to the summons issued to them.
Hence, no such circumstances the apprehension raised by the present petitioners appears to be genuine apprehension.
In view of the above discussion, instant anticipatory application filed by the present petitioner namely, (1) Sahid Ali @ Nur Sahidulla, and (2) Habej Ali @ Hafizur Rahman @ Habijur Rahman is hereby disposed of with the observation that the present petitioners shall appear before the Court of learned SDJM (S), Darrang, Mangaldoi within a period of 15 days from the date of this order and if they do so, they shall be allowed to go on bail of Rs. 30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the learned SDJM (S), Darrang, Mangaldoi, subject to the condition:
Page No.# 5/5 1. That the petitioners shall appears before the Committal Court and learned Trial Court as and when so directed by the said Courts and shall co-operate in their trial.
2. The petitioners shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat, or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case, so as to dissuade him or her from disclosing such facts to the Courts.
With the above observation, this instant anticipatory bail application is hereby disposed of.

sentences.text: Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

sentences.text: In what cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may be exercised where the offender and victim have settled their dispute would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case and no category can be prescribed.

sentences.text: However, before exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.

sentences.text: Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.

sentences.text: Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society.

It will not be just enough for the court to look into the averments made in the FIR/ complaint alone for the purpose of ascertaining whether the necessary ingredients to constitute the alleged offence are disclosed or not.
ii. In frivolous or vexatious proceedings, the court owes a duty to look into many other attending circumstances emerging from the record of the case over and above the averments made.
iii. The overall circumstances leading to the initiation/ registration of the case as well as the materials collected in the course of investigation is to be looked into.
11. From the reading of the FIR in its entirety and if it is taken on face value, it cannot be said that the allegations are omnibus allegations, rather a specific statement is made how the alleged offences were committed
12. It is by now well settled that while exercising its power under section 482 Cr
. P.C., this court cannot enter into such disputed factual aspect, though this court will not be powerless in a given case to examine the detailed materials available on record to look into whether the application was filed with malafide intention or to harass the petitioner.
13. This court do not find anything to suggest that the FIR was filed with a malafide intention, rather the case of the petitioner that it was filed with malafide intention rest on some factual assertions which cannot be entertained by this petition under section 482 Cr.P.C.
14.

15. The interim order, if any, passed earlier stands vacated.
